title: Machu Picchu
summary: Machu Picchu is an Inca mountain estate of terraces, ramps and stone buildings on an Andean ridge above the Urubamba valley, tied by colonial sources to the emperor Pachacuti. Radiocarbon dates on burials show it was in use from about 1420 until the Spanish conquest era, some two decades earlier than texts implied.

uncertainty.note: Start and end are the AMS radiocarbon range of c. AD 1420-1532 from Burger et al. 2021; Yale reports the same study as about 1420 to 1530. Textual sources had placed the start after 1438 or as late as 1450.

as_recorded.value: the site was occupied from c. AD 1420–1532
in use from about A.D. 1420 to A.D. 1530

where.modern_name: Historic Sanctuary of Machu Picchu, Cusco Region, Peru
where.historical_name: Inca royal estate in the Urubamba valley, Tawantinsuyu (Inca Empire)

importance.justification: The best-known Inca site, a UNESCO World Heritage property since 1983, and a central image of the Andean past.
